lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹133 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹7 cr vs working capital ₹406 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: 10 dividends in 10 years with no gap longer than 18 months.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +65%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹41 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.

story.what_it_does: ACE makes cranes, construction and material handling equipment, with smaller agri equipment and defence businesses. In FY26 it had total income of about ₹3,390 crore, EBITDA of ₹614 crore and profit after tax of ₹415 crore.
story.plans: Management targets revenue of ₹6,000-7,000 crore by FY29-FY30, against capacity of about ₹5,500 crore. It plans about ₹200 crore of capex in FY27, a tower crane factory, a 50:50 JV with KATO WORKS for heavy cranes, and growth in defence and exports.
story.moat: The notes show a company with net cash (about ₹1,200 crore on books) and no debt, plus steady EBITDA margins of 18-20%. It has passed on price increases of about 10% to offset steel and commodity costs. Chinese rivals are described as aggressive on pricing and credit terms, and the notes do not describe a clear structural edge.

scenarios.story: Demand stays strong after the best-ever Q1 FY27, and H1 FY27 income rose 20% with margins near 20%. Defence, exports and the new JV add to growth toward the FY29-FY30 target.
signals_to_watch: Total income growth staying near 20% in coming quarters
Defence share rising beyond 5% and exports toward the 6% FY27 target

scenarios.story: Growth continues but moderates as rains, high commodity costs and geopolitical tension weigh. Price hikes largely protect margins rather than expand them.
signals_to_watch: EBITDA margin holding near the 18% steady-state level
About 2% of the 11-12% cost impact still to be passed on

scenarios.story: Cost inflation and Chinese competition squeeze margins, as in Q4 FY26 when margin fell to about 16%. Anti-dumping duty never arrives and the cranes segment weakens again.
signals_to_watch: Anti-dumping duty on imported cranes remaining un-notified
Debtors turnover, which fell 22.8% to 11.73 times in FY26, weakening further
